text:
MPC gained 0.44% today to close at $414.65, capping a strong recovery week that saw the stock climb 11% since Nov 6. The rebound reflects a stabilization in refining economics: US crude held steady around $89.62/barrel while US refineries operated at 95.2% capacity, and critically, heating oil prices remain elevated—up 59% from last winter—which supports diesel and distillate margins that are key to refiner profitability. This pricing backdrop has supported the stock's rebound from its week-ago lows even as broader oil markets show signs of surplus supply.

The recovery also fits into a shift in near-term refining conditions. Russia's crude production rebounded in October and global oil markets moved to surplus, which typically pressures crude prices, yet heating oil remains historically expensive due to winter demand concerns—a mismatch that can widen margins for refiners who crack crude into distillates. That structural advantage appears to be supporting the stock's momentum over the past few days.
